title: The Man with the Cocoanuts
year_evidence: 扉に『Philippine Folk Tales / Compiled and Annotated by / Mabel Cook Cole / 1916』
text:
_Tinguian_

One day a man who had been to gather his cocoanuts loaded his horse
heavily with the fruit. On the way home he _met_ a boy whom he asked
how long it would take to reach the house.

"If you go slowly," said the boy, looking at the load on the horse,
"you will arrive very soon; but if you go fast, it will take you
all day."

The man could not believe this strange speech, so he hurried his
horse. But the cocoanuts fell off and he had to stop to pick them
up. Then he hurried his horse all the more to make up for lost time,
but the cocoanuts fell off again. Many times he did this, and it was
night when he reached home. [90]
paragraphs: One day a man who had been to gather his cocoanuts loaded his horse heavily with the fruit. On the way home he _met_ a boy whom he asked how long it would take to reach the house.
"If you go slowly," said the boy, looking at the load on the horse, "you will arrive very soon; but if you go fast, it will take you all day."

The man could not believe this strange speech, so he hurried his horse. But the cocoanuts fell off and he had to stop to pick them up. Then he hurried his horse all the more to make up for lost time, but the cocoanuts fell off again. Many times he did this, and it was night when he reached home. [90]
ある日、椰子の実を集めに行っていた男が、その実を馬に重く積んだ。家への道で一人の子に出会い、家に着くまでどれくらいかかるかと尋ねた。
「ゆっくり行けば」と、子は馬の積み荷を見ながら言った。「たいそう早く着くでしょう。でも速く行けば、一日かかるでしょう。」
男はこの奇妙な言葉を信じられなかったので、馬を急がせた。けれども椰子の実が落ちてしまい、そして拾うために止まらなければならなかった。それから彼は失った時を埋め合わせるために馬をいっそう急がせたけれども、椰子の実はまた落ちた。何度もこうして、そして家に着いたときには夜だった。[90]
